Good meals
Dec 2018 • Family
Visited the first time as among other nearby options this restaurant looked the cleanest, and prices seemed acceptable. So we went in.
Lots of things they'd put on the table without asking whether you needed them, for example water bottles, wet wipes, peanuts, cashew nuts, DO NOT think these are complementary, as they would surely charge you for whatever you consume. They even gave us a new wasabi tube which, upon repeated enquiries, was actually chargeable, even though the dish itself is meant to go with a bit of wasabi. Outright hidden charges they were trying to trick us into. They did provide some wasabi free of charge though after our complaints.
Dishes tasted well and our family did enjoy the meal, so we actually came back the next day. This time round the experience was good, and we had no complaint.
Except that their steamboats, no matter how much they try, will have some traces of chilies. So, think twice if you have kids and want to order steamboat.

Trying 3 times to cheat on the bill with fantasy prices.
Apr 2018 • Family
It's located at the bay between the two last bridges.
Tables are upstairs, design with red paper lanterns.
Walked in because it looked nice and we were very hungry.
I noticed that on some menus prices were unreadable, I first thought that happened by error, but I took the only readable priced menu booklet upstairs to select there.
Staff not 
For drinks we ordered one big bottle of water and one beer "Bia Sai Gon". They brought us 2 small bottles of water and 2 warm bottles of "Bia Sai Gon special" with glasses filled with ice from a big 5 liter plastic bucket.
For our dinner we ordered chicken fried rice for 100k Dong! and grilled tuna steak also for 100k 
The rice was having barely micro pieces of chicken and vegetables in it and lacked seasoning and the common Vietnamese herbs. At every street food stand you get it much tastier and with more ingredients.
The tuna was overdone and dry.
There were no seasonings or sauces on the table or brought automatically, we had to ask for it 2 times.
To my astonishment when we ordered the bill it was 360k.
ALL we consumed was billed with incorrect and higher prices.
We told them to check again with the menu. 
They came back with 340k
Again we asked them to doublecheck it with the menu that I brought upstairs and they came back with 320k.
Now I have gotten a little bit angry, asked them for the bill and a pencil and writing and adding up the prices while showing them each item on the menu very slow.
They took that with them and finally came back with a new written bill with the correct amounts and the correct sum.
I don't know if the restaurants management orders them to do that, if the staff does it on their own accounts to "raise their salary" or if they are too undereducated to copy 4 numbers from the menu to the bill and use the calculator of their smartphones to sum it up.
I really hope that it is the last reason, because I love Vietnam and it's people and don't want to think bad about them, but 3TIMES ERRORS looks very much like intention.
I am sorry for You folks, that I was not fast and clever enough to take pictures of the wrong bills and the cheating staff.
But I have witnesses.
Avoid this place if you are not looking badly for something to make you unhappy and angry.

Great Breakfast
Jan 2018 • Family
Our hotel did not serve breakfast, so a 15 minute walk along Nha Trang beach bought us to Cay Me Nha Trang.

It is a large and stylish restaurant, with both undercover and outdoor seating, which mainly comprises comfortably cushioned wicker chairs.

The first day my son and I ordered breakfast with the works, two eggs, sausages, bacon, tomatoes, baked beans, mushrooms and Vietnamese bread roll. 

It stumped even my son, who has a huge appetite, so the next day we scaled back and I had a mushroom omelette, which I folded into a baguette to make a sandwich.

The coffee here is great and I nearly "caffeined" out with two double espressos.

Great start to the day.

Ok restaurant
Feb 2017 • Couples
We had lunch here. 
The general impression is that this seafood restaurant is very similar to others in the same street.

The place was clean. We sat upstairs with a nice view overlooking that fishing vessels at the bay .

Some staff members had some English language knowledge, others none.

The menu card had no pictures, just text in Vietnamese, Russian and some sort of English. 

We had squid, tuna steak and steamed rice.

The squid and the rice arrived after 15 minutes the tuna steak took about one hour. Taste of both dishes was good although the tuna steak was quite dry. 

We had two small bottles of water and 4 beers. Total VND 475,000 . It seemed a expensive as tiger beers was approximately VND 20,000 and Saigon green can was VND 15,000

Value for money on a 0 to 10 scale is 6
